product.name: PC5
product.identity: An independent engineering project that builds PC-side boot, hardware and compatibility infrastructure toward running genuine Sony PlayStation 5 system software on compatible PC hardware.
product.mission: PC5 is an independent engineering project whose destination is to run the genuine Sony PlayStation 5 system software on compatible PC hardware, and to deliver the authentic PS5 platform and gaming experience there.

destination.statement: Genuine Sony PlayStation 5 system software executing on compatible PC hardware, through PC5's own platform.
destination.evidence_class: execution evidence produced by the software itself (levels[4])
must_not_be_satisfied_by: a simulated or modelled environment running PC5 payloads
an imitation of the PS5 interface
a screenshot without the software's own output

foundation.name: Linux tier (optional host)
foundation.product_surface: the PC5 platform: PC5 kernel and platform services

non_goals: a Linux distribution with a PlayStation theme
an imitation of the PS5 interface as an end in itself
distributing, decrypting or keying Sony firmware, or circumventing authentication
universal hardware support instead of a qualification list
claiming any success level without the evidence class defined for it

forbidden_claims.why: redefines the product as an imitation of the PS5 rather than a platform for running it
same: the destination is the platform, not the resemblance

forbidden_claims.pattern: Linux is the planned hardware foundation
forbidden_claims.why: declares the optional substrate to be the product
the old gate that forbade the mission from being a dependency of the product
the same rule stated as a property of the architecture
the split that made the destination optional
the former architecture, which must not be presented as current
the scheduling decision that demoted the destination

levels.statement: PC5 boots on qualified PC hardware
levels.acceptance: the image boots to the PC5 environment on at least one machine from the qualification list, with the machine named, its firmware recorded and the serial log committed, in a BIOS and in a UEFI configuration
levels.evidence_class: a boot log from physical hardware, committed with the machine identified

levels.statement: PC5 controls the required hardware through its own architecture
levels.acceptance: PC5's own drivers initialise interrupts, timers, PCIe, one NVMe device and one input device and report them in the boot log
levels.evidence_class: boot log plus per-device qualification rows; firmware-provided services do not count

levels.acceptance: processes and threads with memory protection, a versioned syscall ABI, display with compositing, audio output, controller input and a writable storage stack, each with a test that fails when the service is broken
levels.evidence_class: a test suite that fails when the service is broken, plus a recorded demonstration

levels.statement: PS5 execution and system-software interfaces exist and are experimentally validated
levels.acceptance: the platform model passes its conformance suite, every modelled device has a written contract and a test double, and a PS5 user-mode contract is served by PC5 with a recorded trace
levels.evidence_class: conformance results plus a trace of a PC5-served PS5 contract; a model running PC5's own payload is not level 5

levels.acceptance: genuine Sony PS5 system software executes on a PC-hosted PC5 platform model; its own output identifies it; the configuration is recorded well enough for a third party to repeat the attempt
levels.evidence_class: execution evidence produced by the software itself. Never: a PC5 kernel booting, a simulated environment, a PlayStation-style interface, or a screenshot of a menu PC5 drew

levels.acceptance: games execute and play at recorded frame rates on qualified hardware through the level-4/5 stack, and the console experience runs on top of that platform rather than instead of it
levels.evidence_class: per-title records with frame-time measurements, and a runtime log of the genuine system where the level-5 path is the one in use

product.identity_note: PC5 is not a Sony product and contains no Sony software. The identity names the infrastructure this project builds and the destination it is built toward, not an achieved capability: the genuine Sony PS5 system software is the operating system and the user experience, and PC5 is the PC-side boot, hardware and compatibility infrastructure that exists to run it. PC5 does not build a replacement operating system, shell, setup experience or interface to stand in for Sony's, and a PC5 diagnostic or recovery environment is supporting tooling, never the product.

workstreams.name: Governance: architecture, evidence, release discipline
workstreams.purpose: Keep the destination, the evidence and the architecture from drifting apart; own the decisions and the gates.

workstreams.name: Hardware discovery and compatibility
workstreams.purpose: Tell one machine from another honestly: CPUID, firmware tables, buses, devices, and the qualification list that follows from them.

workstreams.name: CPU architecture and execution environment
workstreams.purpose: Execute code the way the target platform executes it: privilege levels, CPU features, interrupt model, timers, virtualisation extensions.

workstreams.name: Firmware and boot compatibility
workstreams.purpose: Boot the machine and hand control over: BIOS and UEFI paths, boot contract, verified payloads, recovery entry.

workstreams.name: Memory management
workstreams.purpose: Own the address space: physical map, paging, protection, DMA-visible and GPU-visible memory, allocation policies.

workstreams.name: Storage and filesystem
workstreams.purpose: Own the medium: sector I/O, partitions, filesystems, integrity, and the storage contract the platform model has to present.

workstreams.name: GPU architecture and graphics
workstreams.purpose: Present graphics: mode setting, framebuffer, command submission, and the GPU device model the destination needs.

workstreams.name: Audio architecture
workstreams.purpose: Present audio: output paths, routing, and the audio device model the destination needs.

workstreams.name: USB, Bluetooth and controllers
workstreams.purpose: Present input: xHCI, HID, DualSense, hot-plug, rumble and trigger output.

workstreams.name: System services and operating-system interfaces
workstreams.purpose: Give the platform an operating-system surface: processes, threads, memory protection, syscalls, device interfaces, IPC.

workstreams.name: PS5 platform compatibility (system software)
workstreams.purpose: Model the PlayStation 5 platform closely enough that the genuine Sony system software can execute on it.

workstreams.name: Game execution and runtime compatibility
workstreams.purpose: Execute PS5 application contracts through PC5 implementations: loading, relocation, NID/PRX shims, syscall surface, graphics translation.

workstreams.name: Installation, recovery and system updates
workstreams.purpose: Install, update and recover: verification, A/B slots, rollback, and the genuine package's installation path when it is lawful.

workstreams.name: Product experience: shell, library, settings
workstreams.purpose: Build PC5's own console experience on top of the platform: shell, library, accounts, settings. The surface, never the destination.

foundations.title: Experimental 64-bit long-mode boot path
delivers: boot/uefi64: a UEFI application that stays in long mode and hands over in it
a PC5-owned identity map (1 PML4 + 1 PDPT + 4 PD, 2 MiB pages, below 4 GiB)
struct pc5_boot64, protocol version 1, with magic, size and per-field validation
ExitBootServices with the memory-map key and a bounded retry loop
kernel64: a freestanding kernel that proves long mode, paging, its CR3 root, its stack and its boot info before printing PC5-64BIT-LONG-MODE-OK
does_not_complete: M2a still requires APIC, a high-resolution timer, a second CPU and per-machine SVM records
no OVMF run and no physical machine has executed this path
no interrupts, no SMP, no process separation, no SVM initialisation

foundations.title: Memory-management groundwork for the 64-bit kernel
foundations.state: partial: page tables and ownership rules only
delivers: boot/uefi64/pagetables.c: identity-map construction, uncached marking, lookup
ownership rules: the loader owns buffers until handover, the kernel owns tables, stack and image
boot-info pointers constrained below 4 GiB and validated before use
does_not_complete: no physical-memory allocator, no per-process address spaces, no protection, no DMA protocol
the kernel does not yet map above 4 GiB, use NX, or provide guard pages

milestones.title: Architecture realignment: one platform, one destination
milestones.advances: replaces the two-track frame that made genuine PS5 system software an optional side project
acceptance: every contradiction between the product identity, the architecture and the implementation is listed with the file that carried it
the destination is data in roadmap.json and is reachable in the dependency graph
the Linux decision is recorded with alternatives, evidence, exit condition and reversal conditions (ADR-020)
the old two-track gate is replaced by release isolation, and a synthetic graph proves the rule rejects an experimental milestone gating a release
make check, make roadmap, make verify and make boot-test stay green, and no milestone that is complete today loses its state
no claim in any document exceeds the evidence recorded in docs/TEST_RESULTS.md

milestones.title: Reproducible BIOS boot medium
milestones.advances: the boot path every higher level stands on
acceptance: make iso produces build/pc5.iso and two builds with the same SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH are byte-identical
make verify accepts the image independently of the writer that produced it

milestones.title: Automated CI and release publication
milestones.advances: a reproducible release other people can verify for themselves
acceptance: a tag triggers build, verify, test and publication of pc5.iso, pc5.iso.sha256 and build-info.json
the published artefact hash equals a local rebuild with the same SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
milestones.blocker: the GitHub token available to this environment lacks the workflows permission, so ci/build.yml cannot be activated (ci/README.md)

milestones.title: UEFI boot path under real firmware
milestones.advances: boot on a UEFI machine, which is the only configuration current PC hardware offers, with a handover that is validated rather than assumed
acceptance: the loader's logic is executed against stub firmware, 58 checks - done
the same BOOTX64.EFI is booted by genuine OVMF, cold and warm variable store - done (docs/TEST_RESULTS.md section 16); NOT re-run under OVMF on every machine, see section 18.6
the kernel reaches PC5-BOOT-OK under OVMF - done
the handover window is validated against the firmware memory map before ExitBootServices (E15) - done, executed against stub firmware (section 18.4)
a memory map that does not fit fails instead of truncating (E16) - done
the kernel copy is read back before the jump (E17) - done
the firmware watchdog is disarmed before handover - done
one physical UEFI machine boots it with Secure Boot off - NOT done
the loader hands the ACPI RSDP over - NOT done (the kernel reports acpi=absent on this path)
Secure Boot support - NOT CLAIMED: no signing key, no shim; the harness asserts the refusal

milestones.title: ATA PIO write path with verified read-back
milestones.advances: PC5 writes a medium with its own driver, which every installer and platform model needs
acceptance: a 4 KiB pattern is written, flushed, read back and hashed
the host compares the image and the SHA-256, and the write is never automatic

milestones.title: MBR and GPT partition discovery (read-only)
milestones.advances: PC5 finds what is on a disk, which the installer and the platform model both require
acceptance: a valid GPT is discovered with the expected partition count
a damaged table reports status=crc instead of a wrong answer

milestones.title: Read-only FAT32 filesystem
milestones.advances: a filesystem PC5 owns instead of one borrowed from firmware
acceptance: the kernel's SHA-256 of a fixture file equals an independent reader's
the image is byte-identical after a read-only mount

milestones.title: FAT32 create with independent read-back
milestones.advances: PC5 leaves a persistent artefact on a medium
acceptance: a created file is read back byte-identically by an independent reader
both FAT copies agree and no cluster is orphaned

milestones.title: Hybrid MBR: the same image boots as a hard disk
milestones.advances: one medium for optical and disk boot, which a PC5 install target needs
acceptance: the image boots from its MBR with the CD detached
a control image with sector 0 blanked does not boot

milestones.title: FAT32 overwrite, directories and 8.3 paths
milestones.advances: PC5 updates its own storage tree, which installation and updates require
acceptance: an overwrite replaces in place and frees the old chain only after the switch
a file written into a new directory reads back after a reboot
a per-write failure sweep leaves no corrupt state

milestones.title: Physical boot and installation on qualified PC hardware
milestones.advances: level 1 of the success hierarchy: PC5 has to run on a real machine before it can run anything else
acceptance: one machine from the qualification list boots the image from USB and reaches the PC5 environment
the serial log is committed with the machine named and the firmware version recorded
a BIOS and a UEFI configuration are both recorded
an installation writes a bootable target and reboots into it
the attempt is recorded with tools/hw_record.py, which rejects an unfilled field, a physical-boot claim without a serial log, and an emulator run filed as a PC boot
milestones.notes: Dependencies M1a, M1c, M1h and M1i are complete, so the only thing missing is a machine: no agent has physical hardware, and the procedure, template and validator exist so that the first person with one produces evidence that can be checked instead of a screenshot. State stays not_started until such a record exists.

one NVMe device initialises, completes a read and a write, and reports its health

acceptance: the kernel runs in 64-bit long mode with paging enabled, verified by a boot log line and a self-test

a second CPU is brought up through the same path, or the absence of one is reported
CPU feature detection records SVM/VMX availability per machine in the qualification list

milestones.title: Memory management: paging, protection and DMA-visible memory

milestones.advances: a system someone can install, update and recover, and the point where the optional Linux tier is removed if it is no longer needed

milestones.title: System-software baseline and provenance record
milestones.advances: establishes what the protected input actually is before anything is built around it
deliverables: the repository-root package as a Git LFS pointer only
acceptance: the pointer's object id and declared size are recorded and asserted by a test
the payload's absence from any checkout is asserted: no Sony bytes are in the tree
whether the package is the full reinstallation image or an incremental update is recorded as NOT VERIFIED until the bytes are lawfully available
an analysis runbook exists that produces hashes and structure only and runs outside the repository
no extraction, decryption or key handling is implemented or planned in this milestone

milestones.title: PS5 platform contract specification
milestones.advances: the destination needs a written platform contract before a single device model can be built
deliverables: psm/ — evidence registry, rule engine, linkage audit and ten interfaces
acceptance: every device class the system software touches has a written contract with its unknowns marked UNKNOWN
each contract names its source (public documentation, observable behaviour, or unknown) and none is invented
the security-state device is specified only as far as public documentation allows, and no bypass is specified
the CPU, memory, interrupt, storage, graphics, audio, USB and service-device contracts each have a test-double interface
milestones.notes: Every acceptance item is met and evidenced: the contract, a 38-claim evidence registry over four sources, a linkage audit and ten PC5-authored interfaces with 261 conformance checks and 16 caught mutations (make psm, make check). It is held at in_progress, not complete, because tests/test_product_identity.py forbids a level-4 milestone from being complete while only levels 1-2 have evidence - the same rule that keeps M1 honest. Nothing here is evidence about Sony's system software, which has never been executed.

milestones.title: Virtual platform core: CPU and privileged execution model
milestones.advances: level 4: the execution environment the destination runs inside
acceptance: the model executes a PC5-authored conformance payload to a recorded completion
privilege levels, control registers and CPUID features are modelled and tested against the contract
hardware-assisted virtualisation (SVM) is evaluated on qualified hardware and the result recorded whichever way it goes

milestones.title: Memory architecture model: unified memory and GPU-visible mappings
milestones.advances: the PS5 memory model is unlike a PC's, and the destination will fault here first
acceptance: a unified address space with GPU-visible mappings is modelled and passes its conformance test
DMA coherency and protection domains match the contract, with a test that fails when a domain leaks
the mapping of the model onto PC memory topology is documented with measured costs

milestones.title: Storage and I/O device model
milestones.advances: installation and boot of the destination both depend on this device model
acceptance: queue submission, DMA and completion semantics pass the conformance suite
the model can host a filesystem the guest mounts, verified with an independent reader
performance is measured and reported rather than assumed

milestones.title: Graphics device model
milestones.advances: a console without its graphics contract is not a console
acceptance: command submission, fences and memory objects pass the conformance suite
the host submits work through the PC5 graphics stack and the result is read back and compared
shader and command-level translation is specified with its unknowns marked

milestones.title: Audio and USB device model
milestones.advances: the destination's audio and controller paths, which are device contracts before they are features
deliverables: platform model audio and USB devices
acceptance: audio output is presented with a measured latency and a test tone the host reads back
USB device enumeration and a controller report path pass the conformance suite

milestones.title: System-services device model: timers, event queues, IPC mailboxes, RTC
milestones.advances: system services are consumers of these devices, so modelling them is what makes service bring-up possible
acceptance: timer, event queue, IPC mailbox and RTC contracts are implemented and pass the conformance suite
a PC5-authored service payload runs against them and the run is recorded

milestones.title: Security and authenticity boundary
milestones.advances: the one precondition that may not be solvable by engineering, studied first rather than last
acceptance: every authentication step in the console boot chain is listed with what it depends on and whether a PC can lawfully provide it
what would have to be true for a lawful path is recorded, with falsifiers
no key handling, decryption, patching or bypass is implemented at any point
the analysis names which steps a platform model could satisfy and which it cannot
milestones.blocker: no lawful trust path is known: the console's boot chain is anchored in Sony-specific silicon and fuses, and PC5 implements no circumvention (ADR-007, ADR-022). Until a lawful path exists this milestone can proceed only as analysis
milestones.notes: The analysis half is published: `docs/playstation/SECURITY_BOUNDARY.md` (2026-11-22) answers all four acceptance items — a 13-step authentication inventory with source classes and confidence, the three feasibility paths and the three falsifiers of `BOOT_FEASIBILITY.md` §3/§4 assessed against evidence retrieved that day (none observed, with the emulator landscape recorded as materially closer than §3B implies), and a per-step platform-model verdict across four layers. The state is **unchanged**: the blocker is the absence of a lawful trust path and a lawful input, not the absence of analysis, and a boundary is not crossed by describing it. `tests/test_milestone_deliverables.py` now requires this milestone's named document to exist, which is the check that was missing when the deliverable was.

milestones.title: Genuine system-software load
milestones.advances: level 5 begins here: the protected input is loaded by PC5's own mechanisms, not by a console
acceptance: a lawfully obtained payload is accepted by the loader and its integrity record matches the recorded hash
the loader refuses a tampered payload and says why
the load path is exercised against a synthetic package PC5 builds itself, so the mechanism is testable without Sony bytes
milestones.blocker: requires a lawful, authenticated input (the M9 payload is absent from the tree) and the trust analysis of M17; PC5 will not decrypt or circumvent

milestones.title: Genuine system software boots on PC5 (DESTINATION)
milestones.advances: THE DESTINATION: the genuine Sony PS5 system software initialising on qualified PC hardware through the PC5 platform model
acceptance: the software's own boot output is recorded from the software itself and identifies a build or version it reports
the platform model is named, its configuration recorded, and a third party can repeat the attempt from the procedure
the evidence is not a PC5 screen, not a model test payload and not an emulator menu PC5 drew
a falsification attempt is recorded: the same procedure on hardware the model does not support fails as predicted
milestones.blocker: blocked on M17 (authenticity boundary) and M18 (lawful input); no evidence of any kind exists yet

milestones.title: Genuine system-software runtime: services, shell and platform experience
milestones.advances: level 6 through the genuine system: the destination's experience, running on the destination's software
acceptance: the genuine home interface is operated with the software's own services and recorded
input, audio and storage behave through the model with measured behaviour
no PC5 component substitutes for the guest's services in the demonstration

milestones.title: Genuine installation and reinstallation of the system software via PC5
milestones.advances: the clean-installation objective: PC5 prepares storage and platform, Sony's installer does the rest
acceptance: the genuine installation flow runs against PC5-prepared storage and completes, with the storage image hash recorded before and after
